title: Module descent on a scheme groupoid quotient, with tensor products and cokernels
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $(U,R,s,t,e,i,c)$ be a groupoid in $S$-schemes with the laws of [def-a1-scheme-groupoid-laws]. Put $\mathcal X=[U/R]$, the fppf stackification of the prestack with objects $U(T)$ and arrows $R(T)$ on $S$-schemes $T$, and let $a:U\to\mathcal X$ be the canonical object. Quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$-modules mean sheaves on its big fppf site which locally admit presentations $\mathcal O^{(I)}\to\mathcal O^{(J)}\to F\to0$ for small sets $I,J$ [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. Scheme quasi-coherence is [pqf-def-coherent], module sheaves are [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], pullbacks are [def-pc-module-pullback], and tensor products are [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Restriction to $U$ gives an equivalence between these modules and pairs $(M,\delta)$ with $M$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module and $\delta:s^*M\simeq t^*M$ satisfying $e^*\delta=1_M$ and $c^*\delta=\operatorname{pr}_1^*\delta\circ\operatorname{pr}_2^*\delta$ on $R\times_{s,U,t}R$ under the canonical pullback identifications. Morphisms are all module maps commuting with $\delta$. This equivalence sends $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ to $\mathcal O_U$ with its canonical datum and sends $F\otimes G$ to $a^*F\otimes a^*G$ with the tensor-product datum, compatibly with associativity, unit and symmetry constraints. Cokernels of maps between quasi-coherent modules on $\mathcal X$ are quasi-coherent and are their cokernels in all module sheaves; the equivalence identifies them with cokernels of the underlying module maps on $U$, with the induced datum. No finiteness condition on the modules and no smoothness or Deligne--Mumford hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06WT (proposition-quasi-coherent), with Tag 06WN (lemma-qc-colimits)(1),(2), Tag 0GQD (lemma-compare-quasi-coherent), and spaces-groupoids.tex Tag 077X (lemma-colimits), whose proof computes colimits on U. The inverse orientation of the isomorphism in 06WT is used here; tensor compatibility is the canonical pullback tensor comparison.

proof.text: Work in the universe convention cited, so that all sites below and all indexing sets are small relative to the sheaf universe. Let $P=[U/_{p}R]$: its objects are $(T,u:T\to U)$ and an arrow $(f,r):(T,u)\to(T',u')$ has $f:T\to T'$, $r:T\to R$, $sr=u$, $tr=u'f$. For a subsequent $(g,q)$ its composite is $(gf,c(qf,r))$; identities are $(1,e u)$. The groupoid laws make this a fibred groupoid. Apply stackification-module equivalence to $P\to\mathcal X$. It identifies all module sheaves and their quasi-coherent subcategories by precomposition, so we may first construct the required equivalence on $P$.

source.place: Tag 06WT, proof, construction of the inverse using 06WR

proof.text: For $x=(T,u)$, the slice $P/x$ is equivalent as a ringed site to $(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$: a cartesian lift identifies every arrow into $x$ uniquely up to unique isomorphism with the special arrow $(h,e u h):(T',uh)\to(T,u)$. The functors preserve the base scheme, its regular functions and its covering families. By the local-presentation definition, a module on $P$ is quasi-coherent exactly when all these slice restrictions are quasi-coherent: the presentations on every slice cover its final object, and these are precisely the presentations required at every object of $P$. The big-site comparison therefore associates to a quasi-coherent $F$ a scheme module $M_x$ on each $T$, recovering $F$ on $P/x$ as $A_T(M_x)$. For an arrow $x\to y$ over $h:T\to T'$, relocalization identifies the restriction from $P/y$ to $P/x$ with base change to $T$; the canonical comparisons in the big-site equivalence give $h^*M_y\simeq M_x$. These comparisons satisfy identities and composition because restriction does and the big-site comparison is fully faithful. Neither argument uses the special form of $P$ beyond its being fibred in groupoids. For the stack $\mathcal X$, also fibred in groupoids, and $x\in\mathcal X(T)$, every arrow $y\to x$ over $h:T'\to T$ is uniquely isomorphic over $T'$ to the cartesian lift $h^*x\to x$. Hence $\mathcal X/x\simeq(\mathit{Sch}/T)_{\mathrm{fppf}}$ as ringed sites, quasi-coherent modules on $\mathcal X$ are those with quasi-coherent slice restrictions, and $F|_{\mathcal X/x}\simeq A_T(M_x)$; steps 7 and 8 use these slices of $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 06WT, first construction; Tag 06WI (lemma-characterize-quasi-coherent); slice identification expanded from lemma-localizing-structure-sheaf

proof.text: Set $M=M_{(U,1)}$. The special arrows to $(U,1)$ identify $M_{(T,u)}$ with $u^*M$. Evaluate $F$ on the universal vertical arrow $(1_R,1_R):(R,s)\to(R,t)$. Its contravariant restriction gives an isomorphism $\alpha:t^*M\to s^*M$; set $\delta=\alpha^{-1}$. Evaluation on the identity gives $e^*\delta=1$. On $R\times_{s,U,t}R$, the universal composable arrows $b,a$ compose to $c(a,b)$. Functoriality gives $\alpha_{c(a,b)}=\alpha_b\alpha_a$; inversion gives $\delta_{c(a,b)}=\delta_a\delta_b$, which is exactly the stated cocycle with projections numbered $1,2$. A module-sheaf map gives a map of $M$ commuting with these isomorphisms by naturality on the same universal arrow.

source.place: Tag 06WT, forward construction; inverse of the orientation in Tag 0441 (definition-groupoid-module)

proof.text: Conversely, for $(M,\delta)$ define $F_M(T,u)=\Gamma(T,u^*M)$. Along $(f,r):(T,u)\to(T',u')$, send a section first by pullback along $f$ to $\Gamma(T,(u'f)^*M)=\Gamma(T,(tr)^*M)$, then by $r^*(\delta^{-1})$ to $\Gamma(T,(sr)^*M)$. This is semilinear for $\mathcal O(T')\to\mathcal O(T)$, hence a presheaf module restriction. The identity arrow acts identically since $e^*\delta=1$ and identity pullback is canonically identity. For subsequent $(g,q)$, after identifying iterated pullbacks, the two transport maps multiply as $r^*\delta^{-1}\circ(qf)^*\delta^{-1}=(c(qf,r))^*\delta^{-1}$ by the inverse cocycle. Section pullbacks along $g$ then $f$ equal pullback along $gf$. Thus the restriction for the composite equals the composite restrictions. The natural identity/composition pullback comparisons justify precisely these identifications. A compatible $v:M\to N$ gives the presheaf map with components $\Gamma(T,u^*v)$, since its compatibility with $\delta$ makes it commute with the displayed restrictions.

source.place: Tag 06WT, inverse construction, displayed section formula; omitted presheaf-functor check expanded

proof.text: The presheaf in the previous step is a quasi-coherent sheaf. Indeed $u^*M$ is quasi-coherent. On the special arrows in $P/(T,u)$ its restriction is $A_T(u^*M)$, with the section formula and restrictions of the big-site comparison. Every covering arrow to $(T,u)$ is uniquely isomorphic over its base to a special arrow, so matching families and their amalgamations are those for this fppf sheaf. This proves the sheaf condition on $P$, and each slice is quasi-coherent by the same comparison. The local-presentation criterion established in step 2 now proves quasi-coherence on $P$.

source.place: Tag 06WT, inverse construction, sheaf and quasi-coherence check using 06WI

proof.text: These functors are quasi-inverse on objects and on all module maps. Starting with $M$, evaluation at $(U,1)$ recovers $M$ by identity pullback, and evaluation on the universal vertical arrow recovers $\delta^{-1}$, hence $\delta$. Starting with $F$, the canonical slice comparisons of step 2 give $F(T,u)\simeq\Gamma(T,u^*M)$. They commute with special arrows by the base-change comparison. Every arrow $(f,r)$ factors as the vertical arrow $(1_T,r):(T,u)\to(T,u'f)$ followed by the special arrow to $(T',u')$; the vertical arrow is the pullback of $(1_R,1_R)$. Thus its comparison is exactly $r^*\delta^{-1}$, and the objectwise identifications are a natural module-sheaf isomorphism. For a compatible map $v$ the maps $u^*v$ yield a natural transformation by step 4. Conversely any transformation is uniquely determined by its map at $(U,1)$, by the slice full faithfulness and naturality on special arrows; naturality on the universal vertical arrow imposes exactly compatibility with $\delta$. This proves fullness and faithfulness as well as essential surjectivity. Compose with the equivalence of step 1 to obtain the asserted restriction functor on $\mathcal X$.

source.place: Tag 06WT, final omitted quasi-inverse verification, written out on special and vertical arrows

proof.text: For quasi-coherent $F,G$ on $\mathcal X$, restrict to the slice at any object $x$ over $T$. The localized-site tensor comparison identifies the restriction of their ambient tensor with the tensor of their restrictions. These restrictions are $A_T(M_x),A_T(N_x)$, so the big-site tensor comparison identifies this with $A_T(M_x\otimes N_x)$. The scheme tensor is quasi-coherent, and the slice local-presentation criterion proves that $F\otimes G$ is quasi-coherent. At $U$ the module is $a^*F\otimes a^*G$; naturality along the universal arrow makes its datum $\delta_F\otimes\delta_G$, using the scheme pullback tensor comparison. The unit is $\mathcal O_U$, since the structure sheaf restricts to the structure sheaf. The tensor identifications are the pure-tensor comparisons in the cited statements. On each slice the associator sends $(m\otimes n)\otimes p$ to $m\otimes(n\otimes p)$, the symmetry interchanges $m,n$, and unitors multiply scalars. Both routes in every constraint square therefore have these same values on local pure tensors. The sheaf tensor universal property makes the maps equal, proving the stated associativity, unit and symmetry compatibility.

source.place: Tag 06WN(2), its slice proof, and Tag 06WT; tensor-constraint checks expanded on local pure tensors

proof.text: For $v:F\to G$ on $\mathcal X$, form $K=\operatorname{Coker}(v)$ in all module sheaves, which exists by the module-sheaf colimit statement. Exact slice restriction gives $K|_x=\operatorname{Coker}(v|_x)$ for each object $x$ over $T$. Under the big-site comparison this is $A_T(\operatorname{Coker}(v_x))$, since that comparison preserves ambient cokernels. Scheme quasi-coherent cokernels are quasi-coherent, so the slice local-presentation criterion proves that $K$ is quasi-coherent on $\mathcal X$. Its ambient universal property is still the universal property in the full quasi-coherent subcategory. In particular its module at $U$ is $\operatorname{Coker}(a^*v)$. Pullback along $s,t$ preserves this cokernel: it is a left adjoint by the module pullback adjunction, and the adjunction bijection transports the cokernel universal property. The equivariance square for $v$ consequently induces an isomorphism between these two cokernels, with inverse induced by the inverse data. Its identity and cocycle laws follow by precomposing with the epimorphic cokernel projection, where they are the laws for $G$. Any equivariant map killing $a^*v$ factors uniquely through this cokernel, and equivariance of the factor follows by the same epimorphic-projection check. This proves both the claimed induced datum and the cokernel identification in the groupoid category. Only right exactness was used, so no flatness hypothesis is needed.
